# Binary bundle metadata fixtures

Apple `plutil -convert binary1` produced Info.plist from Info.xml. The metadata
includes every standard plist value type, UTF-16/supplementary characters,
extended lengths and repeated values. Apple `codesign -s - --timestamp=none`
signed the three apps and accepted each with `--verify --strict`. Executables
and resources come from this repository's existing public bundle fixture helper.
The manifest pins every file, both Apple tools, the host and command arguments.

`TestNativeBinaryBundleFixtures` verifies and reproduces the three signatures on
every OS. `TestAppleBinaryBundleParity` independently compares the native writer
with the CLI for these bytes and a second encoding from howett.net/plist.

For deliberate regeneration, move Info.plist, Info.xml, manifest.json and all
three apps to an ignored backup under artifacts, leaving an empty destination:

```sh
MACOSCODESIGN_RECORD_BINARY_BUNDLES=1 MACOSCODESIGN_REQUIRE_APPLE=1 CGO_ENABLED=0 \
  go test ./acceptance -run '^TestRecordAppleBinaryBundleFixtures$' -count=1 -v
```

Review regenerated bytes and hashes, then run `make verify`. The recorder rejects
an existing manifest; app copies refuse overwrites. `.gitattributes` preserves
fixture bytes. The three Resources/.DS_Store files are public text test resources
and must remain tracked despite global ignore rules.
